rv.q: A promising start for Byrne then – and a triumphant one for Ali.

It is all charming but the high jinks are protracted, the jokes do not always land and some exchanges seem too much like disjointed warmup riffs. The play ends just as the drama deepens and we begin to learn a bit more about these girls – but for too brief a time.
Sharp lines and strong characterisation overwhelm a slightly stagnant story, but Ali keeps the audience laughing.
A truly remarkable and refreshing piece of theatre – when it comes to things I can fault about it, there really is nothing.
It is a perfect example of how the arts can and should be used to create social and political change.

cn.t: Critics praise this sassy, coming-of-age comedy for its sharp writing, strong characterization, and pure pleasure. Ali's Breakfast Club-inspired tale of four British-Somali Muslim girls in Saturday detention delivers laughs and fresh perspective.
